title: What If the Sky Rained 40 Shooting Stars a Second? It Did

scenes.text: What if the sky rained 40 shooting stars a second? On November 17, 1966, it did.
Observers at Kitt Peak, Arizona, estimated about 40 meteors per second, around 144,000 an hour.
The peak lasted roughly 15 to 20 minutes.
Witnesses described meteors falling in all directions like a gigantic umbrella, pouring out of Leo.
One astronomer said it went from rain to hail to storm, too many to count. He shielded his face.
It beat the 1,000-an-hour storm threshold dozens of times over, before dawn washed it away.

description:
What if the sky rained 40 shooting stars a second?
On November 17, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm peaked at about 40 per second over Arizona.
